backlog.spec: In solve(), keep two states: 'best' (the best valid packing ever, which is returned) and 'cur' (the packing that kicks start from). After a kick and repair giving sum s_new, accept it as cur if s_new > s_cur, or otherwise with probability exp((s_new - s_cur) / T) with T = 0.002 * (1 - elapsed / (TIME_FRACTION * time_limit)) + 1e-6, using rng for the draw. Always update best when s_new > s_best. If 25 consecutive kicks do not improve best, reset cur to best. This lets the search leave a local optimum that greedy acceptance cannot escape.
backlog.title: Annealed acceptance with reset to best

backlog.spec: Change the kick's starting radii so SLSQP starts from a looser, nearly feasible point. After re-randomising the centres in the disc, set the radii of the kicked circles to 0.02 instead of 0, and multiply by 0.8 the radii of every non-kicked circle whose centre lies within 2 * R of p. Leave all other radii as they are. Then run the same phase-2 SLSQP, repair and greedy acceptance. The slack around the kicked region lets the neighbouring circles shift and the new circles grow together, rather than the new circles being squeezed into whatever gaps the rigid incumbent leaves.
backlog.title: Deflate neighbours of the kicked region

backlog.spec: Give _solve_once an optional maxiter argument. For kick solves (start is not None) use maxiter = 80 instead of 200 so that more kicks fit in the budget. Then stop the kick loop at 0.72 * time_limit instead of 0.8, and afterwards run one final SLSQP on the best packing with the free-radius objective and constraints, options maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-13, starting from the best centres and radii. Repair the polished result with _repair and return it only if its sum of radii is larger than the unpolished best; otherwise return the unpolished best. Guard the polish so that total CPU time stays below 0.9 * time_limit (skip it if less than 3 s remain).
backlog.title: Cheaper kick solves with a final tight polish

backlog.spec: The run currently commits to the single first random start. Change solve() so that the first 20 percent of the usable time is spent on independent random restarts (_solve_once(n, rng) with start=None, each followed by clip and _repair), keeping the best; only after that phase begin the local-kick loop from the best start. Use the same loop and time checks; only the condition 'best is None' becomes 'best is None or elapsed < 0.2 * TIME_FRACTION * time_limit'.
backlog.title: Multi-start then kick the best start

backlog.spec: For each kick, generate 3 candidate re-randomisations of the same disc (same p, R and mask m, different random centres). Score each candidate cheaply without SLSQP: for the kicked circles, score = sum over kicked circles of min(distance to nearest wall, half the distance to the nearest other kicked centre, min over non-kicked circles of (distance to centre - radius)), with negative terms kept negative. Run the phase-2 SLSQP only on the candidate with the highest score. Everything else (radii of kicked circles set to 0, repair, greedy acceptance) stays unchanged. The scoring is a few numpy lines and costs far less than one SLSQP call, so it filters out kicks that drop new centres on top of existing circles.
backlog.title: Best-of-three placements per kick by cheap LP-free screening

backlog.spec: TIME_FRACTION = 0.8 leaves 6 s of each 30 s call unused. Track the longest duration of any single loop iteration in solve() (process_time before and after) and replace the loop condition by: continue while elapsed + 1.5 * longest_iteration_so_far < 0.95 * time_limit. Keep a hard stop at 0.95 * time_limit so that the 45 s limit can never be reached. No other change.
backlog.title: Use more of the time budget safely

backlog.spec: For fixed centres the optimal radii solve a linear program: maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= distance of centre i to the nearest wall, r >= 0. Add a function _lp_radii(c) using scipy.optimize.linprog (method='highs') with a sparse or dense A_ub built from np.triu_indices, and in solve() call it on the centres of each candidate (or at least on the final best) before _repair. Then still run _repair as a safety net and subtract SHRINK. If linprog fails, fall back to the SLSQP radii. This recovers the radius that the pairwise proportional shrink in _repair throws away when SLSQP ends slightly infeasible.
backlog.title: LP radius polish replacing shrink repair

backlog.spec: Add a stagnation counter to the kick loop: count consecutive kicks that did not improve the current chain's packing. When the counter reaches STALL = 40, start a new chain: call _solve_once(n, rng) with start=None (random start, equal-radius phase, free phase), make its repaired result the current chain state, and reset the counter. Keep a separate global `best` across all chains and return it. Kicks always start from the current chain state, and a kick is accepted if it improves the current chain state. This is one counter and one extra variable; do not add pools or migration.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered fresh chain

backlog.spec: Bias where kicks happen. Instead of drawing the kick centre p uniformly in the unit square, pick one circle index i with probability proportional to (r_max - r_i + 0.01), where r are the radii of the current best packing and r_max their maximum, and set p = c[i] plus Gaussian noise with sd 0.03. Use this biased choice with probability 0.7 and the existing uniform p with probability 0.3. The disc radius, re-randomisation, SLSQP solve and acceptance stay as they are. The rationale is that small circles mark the poorly packed regions where a local rearrangement is most likely to gain.
backlog.title: Centre kicks on small circles

backlog.spec: SLSQP is run with the default ftol of 1e-6 and maxiter 200, so the returned packing is often not fully converged and _repair then shrinks radii. Reserve the last 2 s before TIME_FRACTION * time_limit: stop the kick loop that much earlier, then run one more free-radius SLSQP from the best packing with options ftol=1e-13 and maxiter=1000 (add optional ftol and maxiter arguments to _solve_once, default unchanged), clip, repair, and keep the result only if its sum of radii is larger than best. Also pass ftol=1e-9 in the regular phase 2 runs.
backlog.title: Tight final polish of the best packing

Local-search walks beat fresh restarts: slot 11 gave -2.6354/-2.6334 and slot 27 gave -2.6341/-2.6324. Replica exchange (-2.6348) and the two-island model (-2.6349) tie the incumbent, so more chain machinery adds nothing. No effect (+0.0000): TIME_FRACTION 0.93, LP repair, warm restarts, successive halving. Hurt: radius-weighted restarts (+0.0165), log-barrier (+0.0045), L-BFGS-B penalty (+0.0034), MAX_ITER 1000 (+0.0019). Start-diversity tweaks are exhausted.
